Byte lengths of an ML-KEM parameter set

Source: R/kem.R
kem_sizes.Rd

Reports the byte sizes that FIPS 203 fixes for one ML-KEM parameter set: the public (encapsulation) key, the secret (decapsulation) key, the ciphertext, the key-generation seed and the shared secret. Use it to check a key or ciphertext before storing or sending it, or to size a buffer or a database column, so a caller never has to hard-code the numbers.

Usage

kem_sizes(level)

Arguments

level

Security level, one whole number: 512, 768 or 1024. There is no default.

Value

A named integer vector of five elements, all in bytes: encapsulation_key, decapsulation_key, ciphertext, seed and shared_secret.

Details

The values come from the native core and are those of FIPS 203, Table 3:

5127681024
encapsulation key80011841568
decapsulation key163224003168
ciphertext76810881568
seed646464
shared secret323232

Hex strings from kem_keygen() and kem_encapsulate() are twice these lengths in characters. Error: level other than one whole number 512, 768 or 1024.

See also

kem_keygen().

Examples

kem_sizes(768)
#> encapsulation_key decapsulation_key        ciphertext              seed 
#>              1184              2400              1088                64 
#>     shared_secret 
#>                32 

# the shared secret is 32 bytes at every level: the level buys
# security margin, not a longer secret
vapply(c(512, 768, 1024),
       function(l) kem_sizes(l)[["shared_secret"]], integer(1))
#> [1] 32 32 32

# check a ciphertext's length before sending it
key <- kem_keygen(768)
ct <- kem_encapsulate(key)$ciphertext
nchar(ct) / 2 == kem_sizes(768)[["ciphertext"]]
#> [1] TRUE

# an unknown level is an error, not a default
try(kem_sizes(2048))
#> Error : `level` must be one of 512, 768 or 1024
